title: Louis's song whistle, slide trumpet and the start of scat singing
summary: Mason recalls the captain's gifts to Louis and how he began scatting when he forgot words.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I think at that time, though, there wasn't all these recording companies like there are now. I think, uh... Uh... The OK and, uh... Uh... Radio Corporation of America was that. I think that's, uh... That was the... The group that was being booked on the Radio Corporation of America. I think they were once... I was booking the band. Hey, you want to talk about Louis a little bit? Oh, yes. Oh, I'll tell you about Louis. I'll never forget the, uh... The first time, uh... The first time the captain brought a song whistle for Louis. And, uh... He recorded that piece of... Not recorded. He used to play that piece of Whispering.

He played Whispering on it. And, uh... Then, uh... He used to play this, uh... Whispering... And, uh... Loves Nest. And finally brought him, uh... He brought him a slide trumpet. Slide and trumpet. He used to play the, uh... Uh... The Warbath... Another Warbath blues.

Da-da. Da-da. Wang Wang. Wang Wang. The Wang Wang blues. That's what he used to play on it. See, the Wang Wang blues. And, uh... That scat... That scat singing that he did. We had a piece once that, uh... Called, uh... Don't Take Away Those Blues. And they had a whole lot of... It was quite a bit of words to that piece. You know, he'd say... Don't take away those blues. That's the way it, uh... Really... The tune went. Anyway, Louis, uh... The captain used to insist on somebody singing. And, of course, Louis tried to sing on it there one day. And... And he got, uh... He got to sing the words. And, of course, he... He forgot the words. And... And that's where he started doing all that... Gobbling up and... And... And scanning. I say... And then it was... It was quite ironic that, uh... A fellow that used to play in the band... In our band, when Louis was there, Was the guy that wrote the piece that, uh... Really started him on his way. That was... That was that piece, uh... Heba Jeebus.
